subject: Can't run my analyses after updating lavaan and semtools - totally lost

messages.author: af5fffcbf63946b8
messages.subject: Can't run my analyses after updating lavaan and semtools - totally lost
parts:
Dear community, 

I'm lost with my analyses after updating lavaan and semtools. I can't run any of my analyses anymore, and I desperately need help. It took me literally weeks to get these models in the first place, and now I'm totally lost again. 

1) First error in lavaan
This was my model: 

sem_fullmodel = "
PBI =~ AV2.9.1 + AV2.9.3 + AV2.9.4 + AV2.9.5 + AV2.9.6 + AV2.9.7 + AV2.9.10
SO ~ a*AV4.2.7 + c*AV4.2.5 + d*AV4.2.8 + e*AV4.1.2 + f*AV4.1.3
PBI ~ b*SO + AV4.2.7 + AV4.2.5 + AV4.2.8 + AV4.1.2 + AV4.1.3+ aid.g + Austria_dummy + Belgium_dummy + Korea_dummy
indirect effect_TV := a*b
indirect effect_MV := c*b
indirect effect_PO := d*b
indirect effect_FB := e*b
indirect effect_IN := f*b
"
res_sem_fullmodel = sem(sem_fullmodel, data=fulldata, se = "boot", bootstrap = 200, missing = "fiml", estimator = "ML", warn = F)
summary(res_sem_fullmodel, standardized = T, fit.measures = T, ci = T)

--> Now, I get this error message: " lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collide with observed variable names: PBI" and I don't know what it means or what I should do. 

2) Troubles with semtools to test for measurement invariance

cfa_SOgirls = "app =~AV2.5.5+AV2.5.4
comp =~  AV2.5.12+AV2.5.11+AV2.5.7"
res_cfa_SOgirls = sem(cfa_SOgirls, data = data.female, missing = "fiml", estimator = "ML")
summary (res_cfa_SOgirls, standardized = T, rsquare = F, fit.measures = T, modindices = T)

res_invar = measurementInvariance(cfa_SOgirls, data = data.female, std.lv = T, group = "Country_Code")

It says that the measurementInvariance function is deprecated, and I should use measEq.syntax instead. I tried, but I had fundamental troubles.  It's incredibly frustrating and I would be extremely grateful if someone could provide me with easy-to-follow help or answers. 

Kind regards
Kathrin

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Can't run my analyses after updating lavaan and semtools - totally lost
parts:
On 9/14/20 12:48 PM, KasiaKa wrote:
> --> Now, I get this error message: " lavaan ERROR: some latent variable
> names collide with observed variable names: PBI"

It means that your dataset contains a variable called PBI. Therefore, it
must be an observed variable, and lavaan does not want to use the name
'PBI' for another latent variable.

Simply rename PBI (in your syntax) to something else.

Yves.

messages.subject: Re: Can't run my analyses after updating lavaan and semtools - totally lost
parts: --> Now, I get this error message: " lavaan ERROR: some latent variable names collide with observed variable names: PBI" and I don't know what it means or what I should do.

Try searching for a solution in the group first.  Entering that error message into the search bar at the top of the lavaan group returned this result (right below your own post):

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/lavaan/jVujbaDAsbc/Kdin7P2JCAAJ
It says that the measurementInvariance function is deprecated

You can still use deprecated functions, they just won't be around forever.  I won't remove it for a few more years, after I build a replacement that doesn't require separate functions for continuous/categorical or group/longitudinal invariance, and does not proceed to fit more restrictive models even when less restrictive hypotheses can already be rejected.  In the meantime, I recommend transitioning to measEq.syntax() only because it is already more general, and has a pedagogical orientation if you use it as directed (i.e., to generate lavaan syntax, which you can then check to verify and perhaps learn from).  

In your case, this is how you could generate syntax for the configural and metric invariance models (adapting the help-page examples to your own model/data).

# configural invariance
stx.config <- measEq.syntax(cfa_SOgirls, data = data.female,
                            ID.fac = "std.lv", group = "Country_Code")
summary(stx.config) # verify the features of this model/data
mod.config <- as.character(stx.config) # save as a character string
fit.config <- cfa(mod.config, data = data.female, missing = "fiml") # fit model

# metric invariance
stx.metric <- measEq.syntax(cfa_SOgirls, data = data.female,
                            ID.fac = "std.lv", group = "Country_Code",
                            group.equal = "loadings")
summary(stx.metric) # verify the features of this model/data
mod.metric <- as.character(stx.metric) # save as a character string
fit.metric <- cfa(mod.metric, data = data.female, missing = "fiml") # fit model
